If neither source-tail nor target-head label incidence holds, both distinct dart labels lie outside the endpoint-label set. This forces at least endpointFloor+2 visited labels, contradicting the explicit near-floor bound.
Target-head label incidence strengthens to literal target=head via first_constant and the same original-source important-target property.
A strict improvement forces an actual newly inserted dart on the new valid minimum path; legality is preserved by insertion. This transfers the incidence statement with no old-distance upper bound.

The first-layer count difference is its actual set difference by monotonicity. Each removed demand satisfies both strict improvement and new excess at most one, so the incidence bound applies.
